paragraphs: Here's what I want you to carry out of this list, friend. These men did wild things, and the passage still won't let the credit sit with them. When Eleazar's hand was stuck to his sword, the text says, "The LORD brought about a great victory that day." When Shammah held that lentil field, same thing: "the LORD brought about a great victory." (2 Samuel 23:10, 12)

Now look at what David does with that cup of water. Three men broke through a Philistine camp for one drink, and he poured it out to the LORD, saying, "Is this not the blood of the men who risked their lives?" (2 Samuel 23:16-17) I would have gulped that thing down and asked for ice! David saw that what people sacrifice for you is not a thing to use up, and he gave it to God.

And then the passage keeps going, all the way down a list of thirty-seven names, with some I can't pronounce even on a good day. The writer didn't skip one, and that tells me God's people are not forgotten, even the ones with no lion story. Even the last name on the list, Uriah the Hittite, is written down (2 Samuel 23:39). So do your small, faithful work in the kitchen, baker, because the One who counts the names doesn't lose track of them.
